# BQ3 classifier for TASK-20260928-57191a. Reads derive_out.json written by derive.py in this session.
# RULE: a row is (b) MACHINERY only if its path lies in a machinery class (identity, approval status,
# provenance/citation, inter-layer governance) AND no sentence of its effective text states an obligation
# on a run (run-obligation keyword scan below, every hit confirmed or overridden by hand in OVERRIDE).
# Every other row is (a) PROTOCOL CONTENT. A machinery-class row with a confirmed run-obligation sentence
# is (a) and that sentence is quoted.
import json, re, sys
d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
IDENT = r'(id|experiment_id|hypothesis_id|question_id|goal_id|batch_id|producer_task|producer_snapshot|review_plan_id|decision_id|decision_id_note|recorded_at|kind|status|version|title|derived_from_idea|source_idea_ids( item \d+)?|assigned_to|predecessor_amendment|predecessor_status)'
MACH = [
    r'^(typed|narrow|gated|v1):' + IDENT + r'$',
    r':approval(\.|$)', r'^v1:(approved_by|approval_decision|approval_basis|frozen|execution_authorized|scientific_execution_authorized|evidence_eligible|execution_admission\.currently_admitted)$',
    r':cites( item \d+)?$', r':design_record$', r':defect$', r'^v1:derivation_provenance\.', r'\.carried_from$', r'\.new_in_this_amendment$',
    r'\.changed_from_d1d10_with_reason$', r'\.changes_from_d1d10_with_reason$', r'\.provenance_note$', r'\.provenance$', r'\.criterion_provenance$',
    r'\.item$', r'\.adds_to$', r'\.replaces$', r'\.how_K_was_resolved$', r'\.not_edited$',
    r':supersedes_fields( item \d+)?$', r':supersedes_fields_note$', r':not_superseded( item \d+)?$', r':does_not_rewrite( item \d+)?$',
    r':does_not_rehabilitate( item \d+)?$', r':governs_nothing( item \d+)?$', r':incorporates(_by_hash)?\.', r':envelope_not_incorporated\.',
    r':narrow_envelope_not_incorporated\.', r':custody_consequences\.', r':precedence$', r':reading_of_self_references$',
    r':governing_text_table$', r':path_additions item \d+$', r':non_claims( item \d+)?$', r'^file:', r'^typed:recorded_at$',
    r':span_rules\[[^\]]+\] except \.replacement$', r'\.declared_builds\.', r':corrective\.declared_not_superseded',
    r':corrective\.reviewer_convention_zero_runs\.item$',
    r':authorization$', r'\.expression_provenance$', r'preregistered_prediction\.source$', r':span_rules\[[^\]]+\]$', r':gated_span_rules\[[^\]]+\]$',
]
KW = re.compile(r"\b(must|stops?|stopped|fails?|FAILS|invalid\w*|gates?|outcome|refus\w*|evidence-integrity|admission|executor|launch|abort|no run|a run|the run|rel(y|ies) on)\b", re.I)
# Hand decisions on keyword hits in machinery-class rows: True = confirmed run obligation (-> a), False = not (stays b).
OVERRIDE = json.load(open(sys.argv[3])) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else {}

def text_of(r):
    v = r.get('effective_text')
    if 'assembled_whole' in r and r.get('my_layer') not in ('narrow-by-hash', 'gated') and 'outside' in r['field']:
        v = r['outside_concatenated']
    return v if isinstance(v, str) else json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)

def sentences(s):
    return [x.strip() for x in re.split(r'(?<=[.;:])\s+', s) if x.strip()]

out, review = [], []
for r in d['rows']:
    f = r['field']
    mach = any(re.search(p, f) for p in MACH)
    txt = text_of(r) if r.get('effective_text') is not None or 'outside_pieces' in r else ''
    hits = [s for s in sentences(txt) if KW.search(s)] if mach else []
    key = str(r['row'])
    if not mach:
        cls, quote, why = 'a', None, 'path not in a machinery class; effective text is a rule, definition, parameter, control, pin or other run-read content'
    elif key in OVERRIDE and OVERRIDE[key].get('force'):
        dec = OVERRIDE[key]
        if dec['run_obligation']:
            cls, quote, why = 'a', dec['quote'], 'machinery-class path mixed with a run obligation (hand decision): ' + dec['why']
        else:
            cls, quote, why = 'b', None, 'machinery-class path; hand decision: ' + dec['why']
    elif not hits:
        cls, quote, why = 'b', None, 'machinery-class path; no run-obligation sentence'
    else:
        dec = OVERRIDE.get(key)
        if dec is None:
            review.append(dict(row=r['row'], field=f, hits=hits[:4]))
            cls, quote, why = 'UNREVIEWED', hits[0], 'keyword hit awaiting hand decision'
        elif dec.get('run_obligation'):
            cls, quote, why = 'a', dec.get('quote') or hits[0], 'machinery-class path mixed with a run obligation: ' + dec.get('why', '')
        else:
            cls, quote, why = 'b', None, 'machinery-class path; keyword hits are not run obligations: ' + dec.get('why', '')
    if r.get('effective_text') is None and 'outside_pieces' not in r and not f.startswith('file:') and r.get('governing_file') == 'none':
        cls, why = 'b', 'no effective text (field not incorporated, no field of the same role)'
    if r.get('effective_text') is None and ('retired' in json.dumps(r.get('replacement_location')) or 'removed' in json.dumps(r.get('replacement_location'))):
        cls, why = 'b', 'no effective text: retired/removed by typed supersedes_fields; the retirement itself lives in typed supersedes_fields'
    out.append(dict(row=r['row'], field=f, bq3_class=cls, mixed_quote=quote, reason=why))
json.dump(dict(classes=out, review=review), open(sys.argv[2], 'w'), indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
from collections import Counter
print(Counter(x['bq3_class'] for x in out), 'review', len(review))

rows.effective_text: (NIST SP 800-186, derived text inputs/SAFECURVES-20260825/specs/sp800-186.txt.) BLOCK: from the first line whose stripped content equals the section number given for the row (for example "3.2.1.3.") to, exclusive, the next line whose stripped content matches the regular expression ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*\.$ . LABEL LINE for label L (L is p, h or n): the first line in the block whose content, after removing leading whitespace-set characters, begins with the two characters "L:". SPAN: from the character after "L:" to, exclusive, the earlier of (a) the first "(" character after "L:" and (b) the start of the next line in the block whose stripped content matches ^[A-Za-z]{1,4}: . DECIMAL FORM: the span with the whitespace set and backslashes removed; it is CLEAN if it is non-empty and consists of decimal digits only, otherwise CONTAMINATED (for example a printed expression whose superscripts or minus signs were lost, or interleaved page text) and it is then ignored and recorded as contaminated. HEX FORM: exists only if case (a) ended the span and, after that "(" and with the whitespace set removed, the next three characters are "=0x"; it runs from after "=0x" to, exclusive, the first ")" after it; with the whitespace set removed it is CLEAN if non-empty and hex digits only, otherwise CONTAMINATED and ignored. VALUE: if the hex form is clean, the value is its base-16 integer V. The decimal form is then compared only if it is clean AND has exactly as many digits as the decimal expansion of V: in that case it must equal V, else locator_failure. A clean decimal form with a different digit count is a printed expression whose operators were lost in the derived text (for example an exponent expression printed without its superscript and minus sign); it is recorded as decimal_span_not_a_literal and ignored. If the hex form is absent or contaminated and the decimal form is clean, the value is the decimal integer. If neither is clean, locator_failure. Which representation was used, and every ignored span with its reason, is recorded.

rows.effective_text: (entry 3.) Every row, cross-source or C-FIELD comparison that reads a derived .txt file (sp800-186.txt or sec2-v2.txt) is digit-checked against the authoritative PDF named in inputs/SAFECURVES-20260825/source_record.yaml (sp800-186.pdf, sec2-v2.pdf), whose sha256 is bound above. PROCEDURE: extract the text of every page of the PDF with pypdf (tools_and_admission) as "\n".join(page.extract_text() for page in PdfReader(path).pages); remove the whitespace set and backslashes; lowercase. Take the value's digit string exactly as the .txt span printed it (the clean hex or clean decimal form used, whitespace and backslashes removed, leading zeros as printed), lowercased. The check PASSES if and only if that string occurs as a contiguous substring of the normalized PDF text. A FAIL makes the row UNPINNED with reason pdf_digit_mismatch (or, for a cross-source, a cross-source failure). The extracted normalized text is archived as sources/<pdf-name>.normalized.txt with its sha256, and every verdict is written to pdf_check.json.
union_with_additions: (entry 3.) Every row, cross-source or C-FIELD comparison that reads a derived .txt file (sp800-186.txt or sec2-v2.txt) is digit-checked against the authoritative PDF named in inputs/SAFECURVES-20260825/source_record.yaml (sp800-186.pdf, sec2-v2.pdf), whose sha256 is bound above. PROCEDURE: extract the text of every page of the PDF with pypdf (tools_and_admission) as "\n".join(page.extract_text() for page in PdfReader(path).pages); remove the whitespace set and backslashes; lowercase. Take the value's digit string exactly as the .txt span printed it (the clean hex or clean decimal form used, whitespace and backslashes removed, leading zeros as printed), lowercased. The check PASSES if and only if that string occurs as a contiguous substring of the normalized PDF text. A FAIL makes the row UNPINNED with reason pdf_digit_mismatch (or, for a cross-source, a cross-source failure). The extracted normalized text is archived as sources/<pdf-name>.normalized.txt with its sha256, and every verdict is written to pdf_check.json.

union_with_additions.declaration: The check is a substring test and is kept as written, not made positional. Its weakness is declared: for a printed digit string that is short (a cofactor h of one or two digits, for example), occurrence somewhere in the normalized PDF text is near certain and the check then has almost no discriminating power. A PASS on a string shorter than 20 characters is recorded in pdf_check.json with its length and is not read as evidence that the value was checked against the PDF. The value itself stays governed by its parse rule and, where it applies, by the hasse clause of the confounder check.

rows.effective_text: J. H. Cheon, Security Analysis of the Strong Diffie-Hellman Problem, EUROCRYPT 2006, LNCS 4004. Theorem 1: for d | p - 1, given g, g^alpha and g^(alpha^d), alpha is computed in O(log p * (sqrt((p-1)/d) + sqrt(d))) group operations. Theorem 2 (the theorem statement, not the 2006 abstract, whose "i = 0, 1, ..., d" is not followed): for d | p + 1, given the 2d consecutive powers g^(alpha^i), i = 1..2d, alpha is computed in O(log p * (sqrt((p+1)/d) + d)) group operations. Here p is the prime group order, called r in this experiment. The J. Cryptology 2010 version (Discrete Logarithm Problems with Auxiliary Inputs) states the same leading expressions with an Exp_G(p) factor, the linear d term on p + 1, and i = 1..2d.

span_check.span_text: An alarm return (PARI error e_ALARM) means the call timed out; the part stays unfactored and the timeout is recorded.

rows.assembled_whole: F2 (in-process PARI): each call is issued as the GP expression alarm(A, factor(n)) with A = floor(R) seconds; if floor(R) < 1 the call is not made and the part stays unfactored. The call is evaluated by the cypari2 Pari instance of corrective.tools.certificate_and_factoring_library.stack_allocation, as p("alarm(A, factor(n))") with A and n written in decimal. RECOGNITION, in this order: (i) if the call raises cysignals.signals.AlarmInterrupt, caught by naming that class, the call timed out (that class derives from KeyboardInterrupt, not from Exception, so a handler for Exception does not catch it); (ii) if the call returns a PARI object of type t_ERROR whose errname is e_ALARM (the gp-interface form of the same event), the call timed out; in case (i) or (ii) the part stays unfactored and the timeout is recorded together with which form was observed; (iii) if the call returns an object of type t_MAT, the call completed and that matrix is its factorization; (iv) any other exception, any other return type, or termination of the process by a signal is a crash under stopping_rules (memory protection or crash), never a timeout. After (i) or (ii) the same Pari instance serves later calls; admission item (3) checks that it remains usable. F3 (GMP-ECM subprocess): each subprocess is started with a hard timeout of R seconds (killed on expiry, which is recorded). Any overrun of an alarm or kill beyond R is charged to the integer, is recorded, and is never refunded. No other timeout mechanism is used.

rows.effective_text: F0 trial division of m_b by every prime below 2^24. F1 every remaining part is tested for being a perfect power (and split if so) and screened for primality; prime parts go to certification and leave the pipeline. F2 every composite part of at most 272 bits goes to PARI factor() under the F2 timeout above; parts are processed in ascending size. F3 every composite part of more than 272 bits goes to GMP-ECM, run over the B1 ladder in ascending order with the fixed number of curves per level below, invoked as "ecm -one -c <curves> <B1>" with the part on standard input, repeating the last level if the ladder completes. After each ECM subprocess returns, every factor it reports that divides the part is split off; every resulting piece re-enters F1, and any composite piece of at most 272 bits goes to F2. For a piece that remains above 272 bits the ladder resumes at the level where it stopped, counting the curves already run at that level. The 272-bit value routes a part between two methods; it never ends the budget.

rows.effective_text: A NEW library-free module, experiments/EXP-AUXIN-7e2e3d/implementation/typed/cert_verify.py, importing only the Python standard library (checked by the AST import audit at admission). It shares no code with PARI, GMP-ECM, FLINT, pypdf or sympy. Its version is the sha256 of its bytes at the launch commit. It checks. (i) Pratt: the listed prime powers multiply to p - 1; a^(p-1) = 1 mod p; a^((p-1)/f) != 1 mod p for each listed prime f; each f carries its own valid certificate. (ii) ECPP step with (N, t, s, a4, P = (x, y)): gcd(N, 6) = 1; m = N + 1 - t; s divides m and q = m/s; b = y^2 - x^3 - a4*x mod N; gcd(4*a4^3 + 27*b^2, N) = 1; [m]P is the point at infinity and [s]P is an affine point whose denominators are invertible mod N, both by exact arithmetic mod N; q > (c + 1)^2 where c is the least integer with c^4 >= N; the next step's N equals q; the chain's terminal q carries a valid Pratt certificate. (iii) Compositeness witnesses: the recorded base a is the smallest integer a >= 2 for which C fails the strong probable-prime test to base a (such a base exists for every odd composite C, including Carmichael numbers); the verifier re-runs that strong test. An even composite part has witness 2 recorded as "even". This arithmetic runs on auxiliary curves over Z/NZ for primality proofs only; it involves no curve of the frozen list and no auxiliary-input power.

effective_text.parse: Standard output, split on LF with the final empty string after the last LF dropped, must be exactly three lines. Line 1 is the cypari2 distribution version and line 3 the PARI library version; each must fully match [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ . Line 2 is the cysignals distribution version, recorded as printed. The distribution version comes from importlib.metadata and the PARI version from Pari.version(), whose first three entries are the PARI version integers.

(1) Each named tool is present, its exact version_command output is recorded, and the parsed version meets the minimum. (2) ECM self-test: printf '(2^31-1)*(2^89-1)\n' | ecm -one -c 25 2000 reports the factor 2^31-1 (decimal) within 600 seconds. (3) PARI alarm self-test: the program corrective.tools.alarm_self_test_program is run as a CHILD process, python3 -I -c "<program>", with the admitted interpreter, and the child is killed if it has not exited 10 seconds of wall clock after it was started. The item PASSES if and only if the child exits with status 0 within those 10 seconds and its standard output, split on LF with the final empty string after the last LF dropped, is exactly the three lines ALARM, ALARM, 4. Any other exit status (including death by a signal), a kill, or any other output FAILS the item. (4) Certificate self-test: path A produces certificates for 2^89 - 1 and 2^607 - 1 and the independent verifier accepts both. (5) Tamper self-test: the verifier REJECTS the certificate of 2^89 - 1 with its top N replaced by 2^89 + 1. (6) The AST import audit of every module under implementation/typed/ passes change.D8_custody.import_rule, and cert_verify.py and every path B module import only the standard library. (7) The five governing-text hashes of change.D8_custody.trial_plan match trial-plan.json. (8) pdf_digit_check machinery self-test: the normalized text of sp800-186.pdf contains the string "discretelogarithm" (lowercase, whitespace removed).

rows.effective_text: Stated in advance, each by an argument from the recipe alone. (a) ROUTING. f1, f2, f3, f4 and w all exceed 2^24, so F0 removes only 2^2 * 3 from r + 1, and the remaining part f1*f2*f3*f4*w has more than 272 bits (its log2 is about B_L - log2(12), far above 272), so the pipeline must send it to F3. (b) MINIMISER. D_L lies in [x_L, x_L * (1 + 2^-19)), because D_L = G * f4 >= G * y >= x_L and D_L < G * (y + 2^24) <= x_L + G * (1 + 2^24), where G is about 2^129 and x_L is about 2^172. And (r + 1)/4 differs from M_L/4 by a relative amount below 2^-290 (w < w0 + 2^48). So D_L is within a relative 2^-18 of the T_plus optimum x = ((r + 1)/4)^(1/3). Write T_plus(t*x) = x * (2/sqrt(t) + t), minimised only at t = 1 with value 3x. Every divisor of r + 1 is s * (product of a subset of {f1, f2, f3, f4}) * w^c with s | 12 and c in {0, 1}. With c = 1 the divisor exceeds w, which is above 2^300, so T_plus > 2^300. With c = 0 and at most three of the f_i, the divisor is below 12 * 2^133, so t < 2^-35 and T_plus > 2^17 * x. With all four f_i the divisor is s * D_L, with t within 2^-18 of s, and 2/sqrt(t) + t is least at s = 1 (value 3 + O(2^-36)), against at least 2/sqrt(2) + 2 > 3.41 for s >= 2. Hence the plus minimiser is D_L, uniquely, and e_plus - F_plus is below 10^-6 by a wide margin. (c) MINUS BRANCH. r - 1 = 2q with q prime, so the minimiser is the smaller member of the tied pair {2, q}, and its depth is below 1/4 by the same inequality as C-BOUND BND-2 (argument there).

union_with_additions.rule: The null-arm bit classes are the exact bit lengths of the PINNED deployed r (held text). effective_text.producing_library: PARI/GP through cypari2. For each prime p >= 2^64: an ECPP certificate from primecert(p), checked on the producing side by primecertisvalid. For each prime p < 2^64, and for the terminal prime of every ECPP chain: a Pratt certificate, built by path A from the complete factorization of p - 1 (recursively, to the leaf 2) with a witness a. PARI's primecert returns a bare integer, not a certificate, for p < 2^64; that return is never treated as a certificate.
effective_text.independent_verifier: A NEW library-free module, experiments/EXP-AUXIN-7e2e3d/implementation/typed/cert_verify.py, importing only the Python standard library (checked by the AST import audit at admission). It shares no code with PARI, GMP-ECM, FLINT, pypdf or sympy. Its version is the sha256 of its bytes at the launch commit. It checks. (i) Pratt: the listed prime powers multiply to p - 1; a^(p-1) = 1 mod p; a^((p-1)/f) != 1 mod p for each listed prime f; each f carries its own valid certificate. (ii) ECPP step with (N, t, s, a4, P = (x, y)): gcd(N, 6) = 1; m = N + 1 - t; s divides m and q = m/s; b = y^2 - x^3 - a4*x mod N; gcd(4*a4^3 + 27*b^2, N) = 1; [m]P is the point at infinity and [s]P is an affine point whose denominators are invertible mod N, both by exact arithmetic mod N; q > (c + 1)^2 where c is the least integer with c^4 >= N; the next step's N equals q; the chain's terminal q carries a valid Pratt certificate. (iii) Compositeness witnesses: the recorded base a is the smallest integer a >= 2 for which C fails the strong probable-prime test to base a (such a base exists for every odd composite C, including Carmichael numbers); the verifier re-runs that strong test. An even composite part has witness 2 recorded as "even". This arithmetic runs on auxiliary curves over Z/NZ for primality proofs only; it involves no curve of the frozen list and no auxiliary-input power.
effective_text.changes_from_d1d10_with_reason: The module path moves from implementation/d1d10/ to implementation/typed/ (change.D10_additivity). The check gcd(N, 6) = 1 is added and the compositeness witness becomes a strong-test witness; both close gaps VAL-20260923-c3c90c attack_iii recorded (the omitted gcd check and the Carmichael case). Nothing else changes.
effective_text.criterion_provenance: The Goldwasser-Kilian and Atkin-Morain step criterion, Pratt's criterion and the existence of a strong-test witness for every odd composite are recalled by this design session (provenance recalled, pointer, not support). VAL-20260923-c3c90c attack_iii records a worked soundness check of the step criterion (internal). The admission self-tests are what the run relies on.
effective_text.rule: No prime enters an EXACT branch, and no r is pinned, unless path A produced its certificate AND the independent verifier accepted it. A verifier rejection voids the branch (or the row, for r). sympy is not used for any primality verdict.

effective_text.budget: Each integer m_b (every branch of every construction control, null-arm and deployed row) receives the full factoring_seconds_per_integer = 3600 seconds. Factoring stops only when m_b is completely factored or that budget is spent. THERE IS NO BIT CAP: no integer and no part is excluded from any stage by its size.
effective_text.clock: (F-J1-5, entry 9.) The budget clock is the executor process's monotonic wall clock (Python time.monotonic()), read immediately before and after every factoring call on a part, whether the call runs in-process (PARI through cypari2) or in a subprocess (GMP-ECM). The seconds charged to an integer are the sum of those intervals over all its parts and stages. The remaining budget R is 3600 minus the seconds charged so far.
effective_text.timeouts: F2 (in-process PARI): each call is issued as the GP expression alarm(A, factor(n)) with A = floor(R) seconds; if floor(R) < 1 the call is not made and the part stays unfactored. The call is evaluated by the cypari2 Pari instance of corrective.tools.certificate_and_factoring_library.stack_allocation, as p("alarm(A, factor(n))") with A and n written in decimal. RECOGNITION, in this order: (i) if the call raises cysignals.signals.AlarmInterrupt, caught by naming that class, the call timed out (that class derives from KeyboardInterrupt, not from Exception, so a handler for Exception does not catch it); (ii) if the call returns a PARI object of type t_ERROR whose errname is e_ALARM (the gp-interface form of the same event), the call timed out; in case (i) or (ii) the part stays unfactored and the timeout is recorded together with which form was observed; (iii) if the call returns an object of type t_MAT, the call completed and that matrix is its factorization; (iv) any other exception, any other return type, or termination of the process by a signal is a crash under stopping_rules (memory protection or crash), never a timeout. After (i) or (ii) the same Pari instance serves later calls; admission item (3) checks that it remains usable. F3 (GMP-ECM subprocess): each subprocess is started with a hard timeout of R seconds (killed on expiry, which is recorded). Any overrun of an alarm or kill beyond R is charged to the integer, is recorded, and is never refunded. No other timeout mechanism is used.
effective_text.pipeline: F0 trial division of m_b by every prime below 2^24. F1 every remaining part is tested for being a perfect power (and split if so) and screened for primality; prime parts go to certification and leave the pipeline. F2 every composite part of at most 272 bits goes to PARI factor() under the F2 timeout above; parts are processed in ascending size. F3 every composite part of more than 272 bits goes to GMP-ECM, run over the B1 ladder in ascending order with the fixed number of curves per level below, invoked as "ecm -one -c <curves> <B1>" with the part on standard input, repeating the last level if the ladder completes. After each ECM subprocess returns, every factor it reports that divides the part is split off; every resulting piece re-enters F1, and any composite piece of at most 272 bits goes to F2. For a piece that remains above 272 bits the ladder resumes at the level where it stopped, counting the curves already run at that level. The 272-bit value routes a part between two methods; it never ends the budget.
effective_text.ecm_curves_per_level: (F-J1-3, entry 8.) DECLARED CONSTANTS of this protocol, not read from the installed tool: B1 = 2e3: 25 curves; 11e3: 90; 5e4: 300; 25e4: 700; 1e6: 1800; 3e6: 5100; 11e6: 10600; 43e6: 19300; 11e7: 49000; 26e7: 124000; 85e7: 210000; after the last level, 85e7 is repeated with 210000 curves per repetition until the budget is spent. Provenance: none external is claimed. The attribution of this column to a GMP-ECM README table, which an earlier design session made from recollection, is WITHDRAWN (VAL-20260927-b99738 coverage entry 8 found that it does not match the README it retrieved). The column is a declared constant of this protocol, fixed before any value was seen, and its determinacy does not depend on any external table.
effective_text.ecm_nondeterminism_disclosure: GMP-ECM draws its own curve parameters (sigma), which are recorded per curve. Which composite parts a re-run splits within the budget may therefore differ, which can change EXACT versus BOUND on a deployed or null-arm branch. A certified factorization and every value derived from it never change.
effective_text.reporting: (F-J1-4, entry 9.) Per integer: the list of parts it passed through, each identified by its decimal value, bit length and the stage that produced it; for EACH part, seconds charged in each of F0 to F3; the ECM curves run at each B1 level with their sigma values and seconds; every F2 alarm and F3 kill; the final list of certified prime powers; and the recorded composite parts with bit lengths, compositeness witnesses and perfect-power checks. Certificate generation is timed separately and is not charged to the factoring budget.
effective_text.budget_semantics: A BOUND row means the full budget was spent without completing the factorization. It is not a statement that the integer resists factoring, and it is never negative evidence (core rule 5).

effective_text.producing_library: PARI/GP through cypari2. For each prime p >= 2^64: an ECPP certificate from primecert(p), checked on the producing side by primecertisvalid. For each prime p < 2^64, and for the terminal prime of every ECPP chain: a Pratt certificate, built by path A from the complete factorization of p - 1 (recursively, to the leaf 2) with a witness a. PARI's primecert returns a bare integer, not a certificate, for p < 2^64; that return is never treated as a certificate.
effective_text.independent_verifier: A NEW library-free module, experiments/EXP-AUXIN-7e2e3d/implementation/typed/cert_verify.py, importing only the Python standard library (checked by the AST import audit at admission). It shares no code with PARI, GMP-ECM, FLINT, pypdf or sympy. Its version is the sha256 of its bytes at the launch commit. It checks. (i) Pratt: the listed prime powers multiply to p - 1; a^(p-1) = 1 mod p; a^((p-1)/f) != 1 mod p for each listed prime f; each f carries its own valid certificate. (ii) ECPP step with (N, t, s, a4, P = (x, y)): gcd(N, 6) = 1; m = N + 1 - t; s divides m and q = m/s; b = y^2 - x^3 - a4*x mod N; gcd(4*a4^3 + 27*b^2, N) = 1; [m]P is the point at infinity and [s]P is an affine point whose denominators are invertible mod N, both by exact arithmetic mod N; q > (c + 1)^2 where c is the least integer with c^4 >= N; the next step's N equals q; the chain's terminal q carries a valid Pratt certificate. (iii) Compositeness witnesses: the recorded base a is the smallest integer a >= 2 for which C fails the strong probable-prime test to base a (such a base exists for every odd composite C, including Carmichael numbers); the verifier re-runs that strong test. An even composite part has witness 2 recorded as "even". This arithmetic runs on auxiliary curves over Z/NZ for primality proofs only; it involves no curve of the frozen list and no auxiliary-input power.
effective_text.changes_from_d1d10_with_reason: The module path moves from implementation/d1d10/ to implementation/typed/ (change.D10_additivity). The check gcd(N, 6) = 1 is added and the compositeness witness becomes a strong-test witness; both close gaps VAL-20260923-c3c90c attack_iii recorded (the omitted gcd check and the Carmichael case). Nothing else changes.
effective_text.criterion_provenance: The Goldwasser-Kilian and Atkin-Morain step criterion, Pratt's criterion and the existence of a strong-test witness for every odd composite are recalled by this design session (provenance recalled, pointer, not support). VAL-20260923-c3c90c attack_iii records a worked soundness check of the step criterion (internal). The admission self-tests are what the run relies on.
effective_text.rule: No prime enters an EXACT branch, and no r is pinned, unless path A produced its certificate AND the independent verifier accepted it. A verifier rejection voids the branch (or the row, for r). sympy is not used for any primality verdict.

minimum_version.rule: Admission item (1) requires the cypari2 distribution version to be at least 2.1.5 and the PARI library version reported through it to be at least 2.15.4. cysignals has no minimum version; its version is recorded, and admission item (3) decides whether the installed cypari2 and cysignals pairing can be admitted.

version_command.parse: Standard output, split on LF with the final empty string after the last LF dropped, must be exactly three lines. Line 1 is the cypari2 distribution version and line 3 the PARI library version; each must fully match [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ . Line 2 is the cysignals distribution version, recorded as printed. A non-zero exit status, another line count or a non-matching line 1 or 3 FAILS admission item (1). Versions are compared as integer triples.
version_command.why: No cypari2 release executed at design time defines cypari2.__version__ (execution-transcripts.json, cypari2_builds.*.typed_version_command_as_held). effective_text.admission_gate: Run BEFORE launch and written first into the run directory as admission_receipt.json. (1) Each named tool is present, its exact version_command output is recorded, and the parsed version meets the minimum. (2) ECM self-test: printf '(2^31-1)*(2^89-1)\n' | ecm -one -c 25 2000 reports the factor 2^31-1 (decimal) within 600 seconds. (3) PARI alarm self-test: the program corrective.tools.alarm_self_test_program is run as a CHILD process, python3 -I -c "<program>", with the admitted interpreter, and the child is killed if it has not exited 10 seconds of wall clock after it was started. The item PASSES if and only if the child exits with status 0 within those 10 seconds and its standard output, split on LF with the final empty string after the last LF dropped, is exactly the three lines ALARM, ALARM, 4. Any other exit status (including death by a signal), a kill, or any other output FAILS the item. (4) Certificate self-test: path A produces certificates for 2^89 - 1 and 2^607 - 1 and the independent verifier accepts both. (5) Tamper self-test: the verifier REJECTS the certificate of 2^89 - 1 with its top N replaced by 2^89 + 1. (6) The AST import audit of every module under implementation/typed/ passes change.D8_custody.import_rule, and cert_verify.py and every path B module import only the standard library. (7) The five governing-text hashes of change.D8_custody.trial_plan match trial-plan.json. (8) pdf_digit_check machinery self-test: the normalized text of sp800-186.pdf contains the string "discretelogarithm" (lowercase, whitespace removed).
effective_text.absence_rule: Any failure of the admission gate is an INFRASTRUCTURE STOP: the run is not launched, the probe output is reported as failed_infrastructure, and no other tool, version or verifier is substituted. It is never a result about any curve or about this amendment's mathematics. Provisioning the declared tools is not part of this text; their absence at execution is an infrastructure stop (REVIEW-AUXIN-20260926-2fc87b K-provision), and any executor card for a run under this amendment carries provisioning as a dispatch precondition.

effective_text.applies_to: EVERY deployed row, before any factoring; every C-FIELD case; every construction-control integer; every null-arm integer.
effective_text.clauses_in_order: (1) field_prime: REJECT if the candidate equals ANY member of the field-prime set FP, defined as the set of every field prime extracted in Stage P (by the row's field_prime_label or field_prime_locator) for any row, whether or not that row pinned, and NOTHING ELSE. No C-FIELD expression value, control integer or other constant of this text is a member of FP by definition. A C-FIELD case meets clause (1) only by being equal to an extracted field prime. For a deployed row this includes its own extracted field prime. (2) not_prime: REJECT unless the candidate is proved prime under change.D7_certificates. (3) hasse: applies only to a deployed row or C-FIELD case whose source prints a cofactor h; REJECT unless |p + 1 - h*r| <= 2*isqrt(p) + 2, where p and h are that row's extracted field prime and cofactor and r is the candidate.
effective_text.evaluation_and_recording: (entry 4.) All applicable clauses are evaluated, in the order above, on every candidate; evaluation never stops at the first reason. The result is the ordered list of reasons that fired, written to confounder_receipt.json per candidate, together with the verdict of each clause. The candidate is REJECTED if and only if the list is non-empty. A rejected deployed row is invalid_measurement for that row and is never factored.
effective_text.scope_on_controls_and_null_arm: (conventions.Q0-3.) For construction controls and null-arm integers there is no "same curve": clause (1) compares against the whole set FP, clause (2) applies, and clause (3) does not apply because no source prints a cofactor for them. The expected outcome for every construction control is NOT REJECTED (no reason). If a construction control is rejected, the run stops with outcome I_CONTROL_COLLISION (never N1, never a result), because a constructed control that equals an extracted field prime is a defect of this text's recipes. A rejected null-arm sample is kept, flagged and not factored.

rows.effective_text: For a prime r and a branch b in {minus, plus}, let m_minus = r - 1 and m_plus = r + 1. Admissible d is every positive divisor of m_b, including 1 and m_b. The two branches are never combined: no quantity in this amendment is a minimum over both branches.

effective_text.new_in_this_amendment: RT-20260923-38bbbf RC2 (DEC-20260923-a4c3d5 entry 14). A planted positive whose plus branch exceeds the 272-bit F2/F3 routing size, at the largest frozen size, with a planted divisor made of four primes that trial division cannot remove and GMP-ECM can find, so that the blind pipeline must pass through F3.
effective_text.purpose: Known positive on the plus branch at B_L = 521 bits, under the typed cost, exercising F0, F1, F3, large-prime certification and evaluation.
effective_text.search_start: x_L = icbrt(M_L / 4) (M_L / 4 is an integer). f1 = nextprime_ge(2^43). f2 = nextprime_gt(f1). f3 = nextprime_gt(f2). G = f1 * f2 * f3. y = ceildiv(x_L, G). f4 = nextprime_ge(y). D_L = G * f4. w0 = ceildiv(M_L, 12 * D_L).
effective_text.step_order: w = w0, w0 + 1, w0 + 2, ... (steps of +1 over the integers).
effective_text.acceptance_rule: Accept the FIRST w in step order such that w is prime, r = 12 * D_L * w - 1 is prime, and q = (r - 1) / 2 is prime.
effective_text.window: f1 in [2^43, 2^43 + 2^24); f2 in (f1, f1 + 2^24); f3 in (f2, f2 + 2^24); f4 in [y, y + 2^24) and f4 > f3; w in [w0, w0 + 2^48). r must have exactly B_L bits. Leaving any window is an infrastructure stop, not a negative.
effective_text.tie_breaks: none needed; each search returns the first acceptable candidate in a total order.

Write T_plus(t*x) = x * (2/sqrt(t) + t), minimised only at t = 1 with value 3x. Every divisor of r + 1 is s * (product of a subset of {f1, f2, f3, f4}) * w^c with s | 12 and c in {0, 1}. With c = 1 the divisor exceeds w, which is above 2^300, so T_plus > 2^300. With c = 0 and at most three of the f_i, the divisor is below 12 * 2^133, so t < 2^-35 and T_plus > 2^17 * x. With all four f_i the divisor is s * D_L, with t within 2^-18 of s, and 2/sqrt(t) + t is least at s = 1 (value 3 + O(2^-36)), against at least 2/sqrt(2) + 2 > 3.41 for s >= 2. Hence the plus minimiser is D_L, uniquely, and e_plus - F_plus is below 10^-6 by a wide margin. (P6) Run the confounder check on every deployed r, prove each r prime, apply the family checks, write orders.json, then orders.json.sha256, and print the sha256 to stdout.log. Construct C-PLANT-M, C-PLANT-P, C-INERT and C-PLANT-PL exactly per their recipes, run the confounder check on each constructed r, and write controls_construction.json. Factor both branches of each construction control blind through the change.D6_factoring pipeline, certify, evaluate on path A and path B, and apply every gate. Then evaluate the C-BOUND declared states on both paths and apply their gates. Write controls_receipt.json with its sha256 printed. If any gate fails on either path, stop (N1 or N4).

Sample, confounder-check, certify, factor, evaluate on both paths and bin every null-arm prime per amendment.null_arm. Write null_arm.json and print its sha256. Complete before any deployed factorization begins.
Factor both branches of every pinned deployed row, in frozen-list order, certify, and evaluate on path A.

Path B recomputes every deployed row (products, certificates, divisor enumeration, witness sets, typed exponents, bounds, minimisers, witnesses, depths, bins) and writes independent_recompute.json. Disagreement voids that branch.
Emit typed_table.json with the labelling of change.D9_labelling, the deployed rows, the controls, the C-BOUND states and the null arm beside them, per stratum.

effective_text.bit_classes: The distinct exact bit lengths of the r values of the deployed rows pinned in Stage P. They are fixed by the primary sources, not by any outcome.
effective_text.sampler: For bit class L and index i = 0, 1, ..., 15: label is the ASCII string "AMD-EXP-AUXIN-7e2e3d-20260923-d1d10/null/" followed by L in decimal, "/", and i in decimal, with no padding and no trailing newline. k = ceildiv(L, 8). X = the big-endian integer of the first k bytes of SHAKE-256(label), taken mod 2^(L-1). start = 2^(L-1) + X. The sample is nextprime_ge(start), searched upward by +1; if the search reaches 2^L it continues from 2^(L-1) upward.
effective_text.seed: The label prefix "AMD-EXP-AUXIN-7e2e3d-20260923-d1d10/null/" is the seed. No other randomness is used.
effective_text.pipeline: Identical to deployed rows. Confounder check (clause (1) against the whole set FP and clause (2); clause (3) does not apply, since a sample is no curve's order), certificate, full frozen factoring budget per branch, both paths, statuses, bounds, bins, stratum. A sample equal to a deployed r, or two equal samples, is kept and flagged.
effective_text.reported_beside_deployed: Per bit class and branch: the count of each status and bin, and the sorted list of exact exponents and of witnessed upper bounds. No statistic of the null arm enters any rule.
effective_text.disclosed_sampler_bias: nextprime of a uniform start weights each prime by the gap below it. This is a known small bias of the sampler and is disclosed, not corrected.
effective_text.size_disclosure: With 16 samples per class, any frequency read from the arm has a wide interval; this is one reason no rule reads it.

effective_text: For a prime r and a branch b in {minus, plus}, let m_minus = r - 1 and m_plus = r + 1. For a positive divisor d of m_b: T_minus(d) = sqrt(m_minus / d) + sqrt(d)   (Cheon 2006 Theorem 1 leading expression); T_plus(d)  = sqrt(m_plus / d) + d          (Cheon 2006 Theorem 2 leading expression; Theorem 2, not the 2006 abstract). e_b(d) = log2(T_b(d)) / log2(r). Admissible d is every positive divisor of m_b, including 1 and m_b. The two branches are never combined: no quantity in this amendment is a minimum over both branches.

effective_text.rule: Per CORR-20260923-187ea3 labelling_rule_for_any_citing_record, with the unit statement of CORR-20260923-f5f060. The rho column is named rho_ordinary_input, value 0.5 (the frozen rho_baseline), and is annotated as the ordinary-input cost exponent of a different problem. Every typed exponent column name ends in E_ASSUMES_AUXILIARY_INPUT and names its branch. Every row states per branch the input model, the condition label and the bits of d (change.D2_typed_costs). The table header cites DEC-20260802-204 B032-C7 and B032-C8. The phrase "identical accounting" does not appear in any artifact. The supply condition is stated in the header: every typed exponent is conditional on the named auxiliary input being supplied, which this experiment does not examine (IDEA-20260831-ccb587 unopened).
effective_text.unit_statement_beside_rho: (entry 11.) Printed verbatim in the typed_table header immediately beside rho_ordinary_input, and in the execution report: "The typed exponents are exponents of the leading step-count expressions of Cheon's Theorems 1 and 2. Each step is an exponentiation: the theorems carry an O(log p) group-operation factor (EUROCRYPT 2006) or an Exp_G(p) factor (J. Cryptology 2010). The typed exponents omit that factor and the O() constants, so they understate group-operation counts. The rho exponent counts group operations. The two units differ by a factor Theta(log r)." No artifact, report or citing record states that the typed exponents and the rho exponent are in the same unit.
effective_text.secondary_metric_scope: (entry 12, O3/S3.) The quantity "bits of the largest divisor of m_b not exceeding isqrt(r)" is reported on the MINUS branch only, labelled "arithmetic; on the minus branch it locates the divisor nearest the T_minus optimum". It is not computed or reported on the plus branch, where a divisor near sqrt(r) prices at T_plus >= d and is not a Theorem-2 quantity.
effective_text.applies_to: every artifact of the run, the execution report and any record that cites the run.

A C-FIELD case is not rejected with exactly its expected reasons, or a C-FIELD-MUTATION result differs from its expected reasons. The pin confounder check is falsified; nothing is factored.
Any reported exponent or bound lies below its branch's analytic floor (beyond the 10^-45 slack), or any evaluated T_plus(d) < d. The evaluator is falsified and the whole table is void.

A C-BOUND state returns a status, witness set, witness, bound, bin, bin_at_least or boundary_flag other than the value this text fixes (H-AUXIN-6db354 falsification_conditions item 5). The BOUND rules are falsified and no null-arm or deployed row is read.

rows.effective_text: For every branch of every deployed row, construction control, C-BOUND state and null-arm sample, three fields are reported: bin, bin_at_least and boundary_flag, each with exactly the value given here. EXACT: bin is given by definitions.bins; bin_at_least equals bin; boundary_flag is as definitions.bins defines it. BOUND: let s be the depth of the witnessed upper bound and boundary_flag the flag that definitions.bins computes on s. If boundary_flag is false and s >= 3/4 + tau, bin is NEAR_FLOOR and bin_at_least is NEAR_FLOOR (the true value is at least as deep). Otherwise bin is UNDETERMINED and bin_at_least is the bin that definitions.bins gives an EXACT value of depth s (so a witnessed depth within tau of 3/4 gives UNDETERMINED, bin_at_least INTERMEDIATE and boundary_flag true). VOID: bin, bin_at_least and boundary_flag are all null. UNPINNED rows have no branches and report none of the three. This clause and definitions.bins never give two answers, and no status and bin combination leaves bin_at_least undefined.

effective_text.replacement: The call is evaluated by the cypari2 Pari instance of corrective.tools.certificate_and_factoring_library.stack_allocation, as p("alarm(A, factor(n))") with A and n written in decimal. RECOGNITION, in this order: (i) if the call raises cysignals.signals.AlarmInterrupt, caught by naming that class, the call timed out (that class derives from KeyboardInterrupt, not from Exception, so a handler for Exception does not catch it); (ii) if the call returns a PARI object of type t_ERROR whose errname is e_ALARM (the gp-interface form of the same event), the call timed out; in case (i) or (ii) the part stays unfactored and the timeout is recorded together with which form was observed; (iii) if the call returns an object of type t_MAT, the call completed and that matrix is its factorization; (iv) any other exception, any other return type, or termination of the process by a signal is a crash under stopping_rules (memory protection or crash), never a timeout. After (i) or (ii) the same Pari instance serves later calls; admission item (3) checks that it remains usable.

expected_value_source.text: Gate 1 of controls[C-BOUND] compares each returned field with the value stated in that state's expected block. After spans G-GATE1, G-BND1 and G-BND3, every declared state states bin, bin_at_least and boundary_flag: BND-1 and BND-3 state bin NEAR_FLOOR, bin_at_least NEAR_FLOOR, boundary_flag false; BND-2 states bin UNDETERMINED, bin_at_least NEAR_CEILING, boundary_flag false (held, unchanged). Each stated value equals the value corrective.bin_by_status of AMD-20260927-narrow.yaml gives on that state's witnessed depth: BND-1 and BND-3 are BOUND, unflagged, with depth above 3/4 (each state's held why_fixed_in_advance), and an unflagged depth above 3/4 is at least 3/4 + tau, so bin_by_status gives NEAR_FLOOR and bin_at_least NEAR_FLOOR; BND-2 is BOUND, unflagged, with depth below 1/100, below 1/4 - tau, so bin_by_status gives UNDETERMINED and bin_at_least NEAR_CEILING. Hence the value condition success_criterion.outcomes[N4_BOUND_EVALUATOR_FALSIFIED] reads ("the value this text fixes") and the value gate 1 compares with are the same value on every declared state. No C-BOUND state other than BND-1, BND-2 and BND-3 exists in a run (invalidation_rules item 6 of AMD-20260926-typed.yaml). A reviewer who constructs a further BOUND state to test the rule evaluates gate 1 on it against the values corrective.bin_by_status gives on that state's witnessed depth, so on every BOUND state that bins NEAR_FLOOR bin_at_least is defined (NEAR_FLOOR) and gated.
